books.section: Topic 8.2 The Cold War from 1945 to 1980
Unit 8: The Postwar Period and Cold War (1945-1980)

primary_sources: U.S. Marine Corps photograph, Korean War, winter 1950-1951

source: original; stimulus photograph is a public-domain U.S. Marine Corps photograph, viewed before writing

stimulus.source_note: Photograph: U.S. Marine Corps, Korean War, winter 1950-1951, public domain (PD-USGov-Military-Marines), via Wikimedia Commons.
stimulus.text: The photograph shows United States Marines resting in deep snow beside a jeep during the Korean War. The men wear heavy winter clothing covered in snow, and several sit or lie exhausted along a snowy roadside.

stem: Fighting in Korea stopped on July 27, 1953, when an armistice was signed at Panmunjom. What did that ending leave unfinished?

options.text: Korea was reunified under a single government chosen by its people
options.misconception: Background: the armistice left two Korean states divided near the 38th parallel; Korea was not reunified.

options.text: The United States and North Korea signed a formal peace treaty ending the war
options.misconception: Background: the 1953 agreement was an armistice, a halt to fighting, not a peace treaty.

options.text: South Korea signed the armistice alongside the other parties at Panmunjom
options.misconception: Background: South Korea's president refused to sign the armistice, so South Korea never signed it.

options.text: No peace treaty followed, so the two Koreas stayed divided and technically at war

rationales.A: Background: the armistice left two Korean states divided near the 38th parallel, so Korea was not reunified.
rationales.B: Background: the 1953 agreement was an armistice, a halt to the fighting, not a peace treaty between nations.
rationales.C: Background: South Korea's president refused to sign, so South Korea never signed the armistice.
rationales.D: Background: the armistice stopped the fighting on July 27, 1953, but no peace treaty ever followed, so the war never formally ended.
rationales.general:
1. The photograph shows the fighting the armistice stopped, but an armistice only halts fighting.
2. Background: the agreement stopped the fighting and set up a demilitarized zone between the two sides.
3. Background: no peace treaty was ever signed, so the war was never formally ended.
4. Korea therefore stayed divided, with the two sides technically still at war.
Remember: An armistice pauses a war; only a peace treaty ends it.
